Police Station: Badarpur

a) Serial number of the case : 95592/2016 b) Date of commission of : 26.08.2015 offence c) Name of the complainant : Tilak Ram S/o Sh. Baljit Singh d) Name, parentage and : Mun Chun Rai S/o Sh. Ravinder address of the accused Rai R/o Prahlad Ka Makaan Village Piyala, Faridabad, Haryana, permanent address:
Village Bishnupur, P.S. Parihar, Distt. Sitamarhi, Bihar.

e) Offence complained of : U/s 279/304A IPC f) Plea of the accused : Accused pleaded not guilty.
g) Final order : Accused acquitted of all charges h) Date of final order : 16.03.2024 State Vs. Mun Chun Rai  BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE  CASE 1.

The present case has arisen out of FIR bearing no.
544/2015 dated 26.08.2015 registered at P.S. Badarpur for the offences punishable under Sections 279/304A IPC with respect to the occurrence of incident on the said date at around 5.45 am near State vs Mun Chun Rai on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62045497/
1 bus stop in front of NTPC Gate no. 1, on the road leading towards Ashram main Mathura Road,
Badarpur, New Delhi.
2.

It is case of the Prosecution that on receipt of DD no. 7A, HC Parminder had reached the spot as aforesaid in front of NTPC Gate no. 1, where one motorcycle bearing registration no. DL8SAG 2888 was found in an accidental condition and one person was found lying in the middle of the road in an injured condition.

Around the same time, one PCR Car reached at the spot and the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL1GC 4489 and its driver Mun Chun Rai (the Accused herein), were handed over to HC Parminder Singh.
The victim was identified by one Mr. Tilak Ram as Bhagat Singh S/o Nanua.

As per the first informant, Mr. Tilak Ram (eye witness), as per his complaint to the police upon which the present FIR was registered on 26.08.2015, being a TSR driver, when was taking up passengers had reached NTCP Gate no. 1 (bus stand) on Mathura Road, facing the road heading towards Ashram at about 5.45 am from the direction of Badarpur, one truck bearing registration no. DL 1GC 4489 came towards the place in rash and negligent manner State Vs. Mun Chun Rai at a very high speed and had hit from behind the motorcyclist who was driving his motorcycle bearing registration no. DL8SAG2888, which was in front of the truck.

As a result,
thereof, the motorcyclist / victim came under the wheels of the truck.
When the driver of offending vehicle attempted to run away with his truck from the place, the first informant noted the registration number of the vehicle and on his TSR pursued the truck.
He then at Ali Mor informed one stationed PCR about the accident, who then apprehended the truck and its driver, who the complainant stated could identify.
He further claimed that he could identify the victim as Bhagat Singh.
The victim was taken to Apollo Hospital who was reportedly brought dead.
The person driving the offending vehicle disclosed his identity as Mun Chun Rai S/o Ravinder Rai (the Accused).
COURT PROCEEDINGS 3.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed against the Accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279/304A IPC.
Cognizance was taken vide Order dated 02.06.2016 and the Accused was summoned in this matter.

Copies were supplied to the Accused and the Ld.
Predecessor vide Order dated 18.01.2017 framed Charge against the Accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279/304A IPC, to which the Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Vs. Mun Chun Rai 4.

The statement of the Accused was recorded under Section 294 read with Section 313 Cr. P.C.
whereby the Accused admitted the superdarinama of the offending vehicle/truck (Ex. A1),
mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle and the mechanical inspection report of the vehicle of the victim (Ex. A-2 and Ex. A-3 respectively), MLC of the injured Bhagat Singh (Ex. A-4)
and post mortem report no. 1016/15 prepared by Dr. Shyam Kishore (Ex. A-5).

sentences.text: The first witness to depose for the Prosecution was W/HC Poonam Chaudhary (PW1) who stated that on 26.08.2015 she was posted as Duty Officer at the Police Station Badarpur and her duty hours were from 8 am to 4.00 pm.
At about 8.45 pm, Ct. Avtar Singh produced a rukka sent by HC Parvinder Singh, same was endorsed as Ex.PW1/1 and the FIR registered was labelled as Ex.PW1/2.
The Certificate under Section 65-B of Indian Evidence Act for the aforesaid FIR registered was Ex.PW1/3.
Despite opportunity, the witness was not cross examined.
6. The second witness to depose was retired ASI Yashvir Singh (PW2) who was the Duty Officer at P.S Badarpur.

He proved the DD no. 7A concerning the receipt of call from the control room regarding the accident in front of NTPC Gate Badarpur (Ex.PW2/1), DD no. 8A concerning receipt of information regarding the apprehension of the truck driver at Ali State Vs. Mun Chun Rai Gaon,
Mathura Road (Ex.PW2/2) and DD no. 9A concerning the receipt of information regarding MLC no.
498/15 with report of 'brought dead' with respect to victim Bhagat Singh S/o Nanu at Apollo Hospital from PCR (Ex.PW2/3).
This witness was also cross examined and discharged.

7. The third witness to depose for the Prosecution was Mr. Manoj Kumar, who in his deposition as PW3 stated that on the relevant date at about 6.05 am he had received a phone call from the mobile of his deceased brother Bhagat Singh regarding his accident.
He did not know the details of the caller who had just asked him to come to Apollo Hospital where his deceased brother was shifted.
He received dead body of his deceased brother from the Apollo Mortuary.

Post Mortem of the deceased was conducted at AIIMS Trauma Centre, where the dead body was shifted and after the Post mortem, he stated that he had received the dead body of his brother vide receiving memo Ex.PW3/1.
He was cross examined and discharged.
8. The fourth witness to depose for the Prosecution was Tilak Ram who deposed as PW4.
He stated that he was a driver by profession.
He did not remember the date of the accident, however, stating that it was sometime in August 2015.
On the date of the accident, at about 6.30 am he was present at NTPC Bus stand Badarpur, waiting for the passengers to board in his auto.
At that time, 4-5 vehicles came from the side of Faridabad, heading towards Ashram.
He saw the Accused driving the truck.
State Vs.
Mun Chun Rai
He did not remember the registration number of the truck.
He stated that he saw a motorcycle was lying in an accidental condition and the injured was lying on the road.
He identified the injured as his neighbor.
The public persons gathered at the place of accident and apprehended the Accused saying that he had hit the motorcyclist.
The doctor upon the arrival of the victim at the hospital declared him dead.

He informed about the death of the deceased to his son,
who informed this fact to the family of the deceased.
The witness correctly identified the Accused in the Court.
Ld. APP for the |State had sought permission for cross examination of the witness, which was allowed.
Witness was cross examined by Ld. APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for Accused and was discharged.
9. The fifth witness examined was ASI Parminder who deposed as PW5.
He stated that on the relevant date he was posted as Head Constable at P.S. Badarpur.
On that day his duty hours were from 8 pm to 8.00 am.
At about 5.45 am, he received a call regarding accident in front of NTPC Gate no. 1 vide DD no. 7A and DD no. 8A.

After receiving the information, he along with Ct. Ram Avtar State vs Mun Chun Rai on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62045497/
3 went to the spot where he met the witness Tilak Ram.

sentences.text: He found the injured Bhagat Singh present there.

He came to know from Tilak Ram that one truck had hit the motorcyclist and due to impact,
victim suffered injuries and the offending truck driver had fled from the spot.
The PCR van apprehended the Accused at Ali Red light and brought him to the State Vs. Mun Chun Rai spot.
When they reached the spot, he saw the injured and witness were present there.
PCR van took the injured Bhagat Singh to the hospital.
He received DD no. 9A dated 26.08.2015 regarding MLC of the victim, who was brought dead to the hospital.
He left Ct. Ram Avtar at the spot and went to the Apollo hospital.
Witness Tilak Ram gave the written complaint to him at the spot (Ex.PW4/1).
He prepared the rukka on the statement of the complainant (Ex.PW5/1) and handed over the same to Ct. Ram Avtar for registration of the FIR.
Investigation was marked to ASI Shiv Ram.
The witness was cross examined at length by Ld.
Defence counsel and discharged.
10. The sixth witness to depose for prosecution was HC Ram Narayan.
In his examination in chief as PW6, he stated that on 26.08.2015, he was posted as Constable at P.S. Badarpur and was on beat duty.
He joined the investigation at the instance of the IO ASI Shiv Ram and went to the hospital where dead body of the deceased was identified by his family.
11. The seventh witness to depose for prosecution was Retired SI Shiv Ram who in his examination in chief as PW7 stated that on 26.08.2015, the investigation of this case was marked to him.
He along with Ct. Ram Avatar went to the place of incident where he met eye witness of the incident Tilak Ram and also HC Parvinder.
He also prepared the site plan at the instance of Tilak Ram Ex.PW7/A.
He seized the accidental vehicle/motorcycle vide memo Ex.PW4/2 and also seized the offending vehicle State Vs. Mun Chun Rai Ex.PW4/3.

He thereafter went to the Apollo Hospital with Ct. Ram Narayan and from there they took the body of the deceased to AIIMS Hospital where his post mortem was conducted and his dead body was handed over to the family vide memo Ex.PW3/1.
He seized the documents of the offending vehicle vide memo Ex.PW4/4 and also seized the DL of the accused Ex.PW7/B.
He gave the Notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act to the registered owner of the vehicle Ex.PW7/C.
He prepared the arrest memo of the Accused Ex.PW4/5 and personal search memo Ex.PW4/6.
On 27.08.2015, he got the mechanical inspection of both the vehicles done and recorded the statements.
He correctly identified the photographs of the offending vehicle Ex.PH-1.
The witness was cross examined at length by Ld. Defence Counsel and stood discharged.
STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C AND DEFENCE EVIDENCE 12.
After the Prosecution had rested its case, the Accused was confronted with the incriminating evidence and his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded.

In the said statement, the Accused denied all the incriminating evidence against him, stating that Tilak Ram is the relative of deceased in this case and a false registration number of the vehicle was handed over by him to police for the purpose of compensation and the other witnesses are police officials who have falsely implicated him.

sentences.text: Accused sought leave to lead defence evidence and deposed himself as DW1, stating that on 26.08.2015 when he going to Mayapuri from Faridabad and driving the vehicle bearing registration no. DL IGC 4489, at about 5.30 to 5.45 am when he reached Ali Mor, he saw that people had gathered while he was driving his vehicle.

He later learnt that Mr. Tilak Ram, who was the relative of the deceased, had given his vehicle number to the police and resultantly, the police had caught him and falsely implicated him in this case.

It was further deposed that some other person had committed the accident and only for the purpose of taking compensation Mr. Tilak Ram, kith of the deceased, had given his vehicle number to the police.
He denied his complicity in the commission of the offence.
Accused was also cross examined by Ld.
Substitute APP for the State at length and was discharged.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 14.
Final arguments of the Ld. Public Prosecutor for the State and from the Ld.
Counsel for the Accused were heard at length and the record has been carefully perused.
I have also considered the rival submissions carefully.
APPRAISAL & OBSERVATIONS 15.

The case of the Prosecution of complicity of the Accused in the commission of the offences punishable under Section State Vs. Mun Chun Rai 279/304A IPC rests on the deposition primarily of witness PW4 on whose complaint, purportedly being an eye witness to the incident, this case was registered.

entities.text: Section State Vs. Mun Chun Rai 279/304A
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: As per the version in the FIR, the Complainant had seen the offending vehicle being driven by the Accused in a rash and negligent manner on the relevant date at about 5.45 am, and to have hit against the vehicle of the victim, causing the latter to come under the wheels of the offending truck.

Contrary to this version in the complaint, the said witness while deposing as PW4 has stated that on the relevant date at about 6.30 am, he had seen the Accused driving the truck and in the same breath further stating that he had seen the motorcycle lying in an accidental condition,
with the injured also lying on the road.
He has further stated that public persons had gathered at the place and had apprehended the Accused.
He had further heard the public persons say that the said accused had hit the motor-cyclist.

The witness was cross examined by Ld. APP for the State, in which deposition he has specifically denied giving the statement to the police in his complaint (Ex.PW4/A) that on the relevant date and time, the Accused had hit the motorcycle of the deceased from behind by his truck and that the Accused was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.

Clearly the said witness has not supported the case of Prosecution as he has only affirmed in his testimony that the Accused was present with his vehicle at the place of the incident soon after the incident, denying that he had seen the incident happen with the Accused, driving the vehicle in a rash State Vs. Mun Chun Rai and negligent manner and to have hit the motorcyclist with his vehicle, resulting in the impact and injuries to the victim to which he eventually succumbed.

The remaining witnesses examined in this matter particularly PW5 and PW7 are police officials who have as per their testimonies only deposed to have reached the spot/ place of incident after the incident had purportedly occurred.

In their evidence, they have stated that they had met the eye witness PW4 along-with other police officials (also not eye witnesses) when they had reached the spot and the Accused was only subsequently apprehended and produced by the PCR car at the spot.

State vs Mun Chun Rai on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62045497/
5

The Accused has also deposed in his defence as DW1 claiming to have only passed by from the place and that he was not involved in the incident reported in which he has been falsely implicated at the behest of PW4, who is the relative of the deceased for compensation.

In the cross- examination of the Accused by Ld. APP for the State, questions have been put to the Accused deposing as a witness pertaining to his employment, terms thereof, the route taken on the relevant date et al.

The Accused has not disputed his presence at the place of incident, however has only claimed that he was apprehended by the police on the allegations of he having been involved in the commission, though falsely.

It is trite law that the onus to prove all ingredients of the offences for which an Accused faces trial in a criminal case rests on the Prosecution throughout and that Prosecution is not relieved of this burden, even if the defence of State Vs. Mun Chun Rai the Accused is weak or doubtful [reference : SL Goswami v State of MP [1972 3 SCC 22].
16.

entities.text: SL Goswami v State of MP [1972 3 SCC 22
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instance case, the star witness PW4 has failed to prove that the accused, though on the driving seat of the offending vehicle was driving the same on the relevant date and at the relevant time in a rash and negligent manner and to have collided into / hit against the motorcycle of the victim resulting in the fall and eventual death of victim.
None of the witnesses have seen the Accused driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and to have caused the aforesaid collision either.
In view of the same, prosecution has not been able to discharge the onus that rests on it for proving the case against the Accused on the charges levelled beyond all reasonable doubts.
The Accused, thus for the aforesaid reasons is acquitted of all charges.

17. Bail bonds furnished to continue towards compliance of Section 437A Cr. PC.
